title: Why Do Politicians Intervene in Accounting Regulation? The Role of Ideology and Special Interests

scopes.description: Full author-documented workflow across the 108th Congress stock-option branch and 110th/111th Congress fair-value branch, including code-document preparation programs, manual source/match stages and all supplied main/robustness branches. Substantial Stata programs are embedded in BDS JAR 2020 Code.pdf, which is not a standalone executable driver.

requirements.description: Author-specific politician master inputs: CONGRESS_MEMBER_FILE, CONGRESS_MEMBER_TENURE_DATA, DW-NOMINATE_DATA and CONGRESS_MEMBER_CV_DATA. They supply member identity/tenure, ideology and career/business variables used to construct the master politician panels; merge keys/field mappings must match the code and must be checked across the 108th, 110th and 111th Congress branches.

Election and special-election inputs: cr1congmem_elec02.dta, cr1congmem_elec06.dta, cr1congmem_elec08.dta and CANDIDATES_SPEC_ELEC_DATA. These supply contest/candidate results and special-election records joined to member IDs/cycles in the politician master; raw field names, election-cycle coverage and the manual special-election construction are not verified.

CONGRESS_MEMBER_SEC_COMMENT_LETTER_DATA is a distinct supplied-code input for the later mfasbsec/letter-control merge. It does not supply the earlier mcl/lastname/firstname/accintcl/prevcl variables whose producer is absent; retain that gap as its own issue.

The manually prepared CONGRESS_MEMBER_CRP_MATCH member-to-campaign/PAC crosswalk is read in multiple politician/FASB sections. Preserve its authored member IDs, cycle/recipient mapping and separate it from cr1congmem_osmatch.dta used in the stock-option branch.

CRP_PAC_DATA, CRP_OTHER_PAC_DATA, CRP_Categories and CRP_CANDIDATE_DATA are separate named candidate/committee/category input tables used to construct cycle-specific recipient/PAC and industry files. Their original vintage, schema, noncommercial-use terms and current route are unverified; historical author wording does not prove current license/access.

The FASB employee-affiliation route first reads the separate prepared cr1congos_indivs_contributors.dta file (no producer is visible in the supplied code), and later uses CRP_INDIV_DATA plus CRP_CMTES_DATA for individual/committee contribution totals. Keep all three source tables distinct; downstream matching uses contributor/recipient/committee IDs, cycle/date and employer/occupation fields as defined in code. Source editions, field compatibility and access remain unresolved.

The author-specific CHICAGOFED_SIFI_SCAP_MATCH workbook/input links SIFI/SCAP bank identifiers and exposure classifications to PAC/recipient records for the fair-value robustness branch. Its manual matches and historical bank/PAC mapping are not packaged or independently verified.

Six separate FASB issue spreadsheets are read by the supplied comment-letter preparation block, tagged by issue and appended into the author-prepared letter file. Preserve them as distinct source issues for the later contributor and PAC matching workflow, including the stock-option branch; the 1101/1102 issue identifiers do not establish Congress numbers. The workbooks are absent from the package.

Keep the author’s distinct manual matching artifacts: cr1stop_fasbcl_empindiv_match_checkDND20180509.xlsx, FASB_PAC_MATCH_1CS.XLSX, FASB_PAC_MATCH_2TP.XLSX and FASBCL_PAC_MATCH_RELCL.XLSX. These are separate checked affiliation/individual-to-PAC and relative-comment-letter match inputs; they cannot be collapsed or regenerated from names without the authored decisions.

FJP2007_Corrected Option Expense.csv is the coauthor-provided adjusted Compustat-items 398/399 dataset used in the 108th Congress analysis. Preserve this specific adjusted source and its firm/year/GVKEY variables; generic Compustat compensation fields are not a supported substitute.

wrds_raw_historicalcompanynames.dta supplies historical company names/GVKEY links used to map Farber firms before the PAC joins. The required name-history period, GVKEY/name fields and a matching WRDS export are not verified.

PAC_MATCHING.XLSX and the distinct PAC_MATCHING_REVISED.XLSX author workbooks provide manual Farber company-to-PAC matching/revision inputs for the 108th Congress analysis. Preserve their revisions and committee IDs; no compatible workbook is included.

IESOCMembers_20032004_firms_PACs.dta is a separate hand-collected firm/PAC crosswalk for the 2003–2004 company association stage; its firm identity, PAC IDs and mapping coverage are not supplied or verified.

cr1congmem_osmatch.dta is a distinct politician-to-OpenSecrets/PAC match consumed by the stock-option branch. Do not equate it with CONGRESS_MEMBER_CRP_MATCH; exact coverage and identifier contract are unresolved.

WRDS_BHC_DATA is the bank-holding-company panel input used to build quarterly bank accounting variables. The datasheet names FR Y-9C; quarterly RSSD/company identifiers, statement items and historical coverage needed by the code require verification. A bounded frozen-catalog search for Y9C, BHCK and BHC aliases found no catalog row; this is a discovery miss only, not evidence that the underlying data or a route are unavailable.

WRDS_COMPUSTAT_BANK_DATA is the distinct Compustat Bank Fundamentals Quarterly source. The local COMPB.BANK_FUNDQ candidate contains the code-relevant quarterly fields; required 2006–2009 coverage, final update selection and the author-file mapping remain unverified. A Compustat annual or generic-company file is not interchangeable.

issues.description: Substantial Stata preparation and analysis programs are embedded in BDS JAR 2020 Code.pdf rather than supplied as standalone do-files, and FILEPATH/RESULTSPATH/workdir are undefined. The ordered producer-consumer procedure is documented in a separate action; recover the sections as working-copy source files and configure roots before an attempt.

Complete source review finds unresolved, absent input contracts across the active code: MABLE/QCEW and agency releases; politician roster/election/letter/PAC crosswalks; CRP contribution/candidate tables plus the separately read, unproduced cr1congos_indivs_contributors.dta input; six FASB issue files and distinct checked match workbooks; Farber adjusted options and manual company/PAC maps; WRDS/FR Y-9C, Compustat Bank and CRSP inputs plus bank identity/PAC links; four HMDA years, two BEA historical vintages, and political endorsement, CFscore, voting, CCES and bill-cosponsorship files. Bounded common-resource probes now verify readable Compustat Bank Quarterly and CRSP daily/index/link-table candidates, but do not establish full date coverage or the author-specific exports/links; retain the two exact producer gaps separately. The section-level producer-consumer sequence is now traced in the run-procedure action; remaining uncertainty is the named input route/schema and the specific mcl, total-assets and 108th-GDP key gaps below, not a blanket unknown workflow order.

The politician master drops mcl and then drops/uses comment-letter variables (lastname, firstname, accintcl, prevcl) without a visible producer in the supplied code document. A later merge from CONGRESS_MEMBER_SEC_COMMENT_LETTER_DATA creates mfasbsec and uses different fields, so it does not establish the earlier mcl/letter variables. Clarify the missing prior data stage and exact table/schema.

The stock-option Farber section filters GVKEY/fyear 2003 and saves a total-assets intermediate but the visible code has no input read before `keep gvkey fye at`; the source, period and relationship to PAC_MATCHING.XLSX are unknown. Resolve the actual `at`/fyear producer and key contract before treating this branch as closed.

The code PDF does not define FILEPATH, RESULTSPATH or workdir. In addition, the September 2007 BEA sheet-2 import contains a literal `3$FILEPATH` prefix, and Table 5B writes under FILEPATH even though date folders are created under RESULTSPATH. The author program must be extracted and path setup/recovery checked in a working copy.

The 2001–2005 BEA/GDP producer maps MSAs to districtcd109 and the stock-option (108th Congress) branch merges that output using districtcd109. The intended compatibility with 108th Congress district identifiers is not documented; confirm this authored geographic key rather than translating it by assumption.

The CAR section comment states an event-window date range that differs from the literal March 11–13, 2009 predicate. Other source text describes a three-day CAR centered on March 12, 2009. Preserve the actual supplied predicate pending confirmation of the intended window/comment.

The 108th stock-option code consumes the former using districtcd109; confirm that authored key’s compatibility rather than translating it.
